packs.title: Quick Wins
packs.description: Eleven free quests you can finish in ten minutes or less.

packs.title: Everyday Together
packs.description: Ten free quests for simple, everyday family connection.

packs.title: Creative Sparks
packs.description: Six Family Plus quests for drawing, making, and imagination.

packs.title: Calm & Connected
packs.description: Six Family Plus quests for quiet conversations and reflection.

packs.title: Move Together
packs.description: Six Family Plus quests for safe indoor or outdoor movement.

packs.title: Weekend Adventures
packs.description: Six Family Plus quests for longer activities and mini-adventures.

quests.title: Reverse Interview
quests.summary: Kids interview the grown-ups about their own childhood.

instructions.text: Have a child in the family choose three questions to ask an adult about their own childhood.
The adult answers each question in as much detail as they can remember.
Switch roles if there is more than one person who wants to be interviewed.

hints: If you get stuck, ask about a favorite toy, a best friend, or a memorable school day.
quests.completionPrompt: What answer surprised you the most?

quests.title: Three Good Things
quests.summary: Everyone shares three small things that made today better.

instructions.text: Sit together somewhere comfortable, like the dinner table or a couch.
Each person shares three small things from today that made it a little better.
After everyone has shared, pick one favorite from the whole family.

quests.completionPrompt: Which good thing was your favorite to hear about?

quests.title: Parent at My Age
quests.summary: A child asks a grown-up what life was like for them at the same age.

instructions.text: A child picks their current age.
An adult in the family describes what their life was like at that same age — school, friends, hobbies, or a favorite memory.
The child can ask one or two follow-up questions.

hints: If memory is fuzzy, talk about a favorite song, TV show, or game from that time instead.
quests.completionPrompt: What was most different between then and now?

quests.title: One-Line Monster
quests.summary: Draw a monster together without ever lifting the pen.

instructions.text: Get one sheet of paper and one pen or pencil.
The first family member starts drawing a monster without lifting the pen off the paper.
Pass the paper to the next person, who continues the same unbroken line.
Keep passing until everyone agrees the monster is finished, then give it a name.

hints: It's okay if the monster looks strange — that's part of the fun.
quests.completionPrompt: What should your monster's name be?

quests.title: Design a Family Flag
quests.summary: Design a flag that represents your family.

instructions.text: Talk about what makes your family special — favorite activities, jokes, or traditions.
Sketch a simple flag design that represents those things using shapes, colors, or symbols.
Color it in together and display it somewhere in your home.

hints: Simple shapes work best — stars, stripes, or a favorite animal.
quests.completionPrompt: What part of your family does your flag show best?

quests.title: Six-Panel Family Comic
quests.summary: Turn a recent family moment into a six-panel comic strip.

instructions.text: Fold or draw a grid with six panels on a sheet of paper.
Pick a small moment from the last few days, like something funny or unexpected.
Draw the moment across the six panels, one step at a time.
Add speech bubbles if you'd like, then share the finished comic with each other.

hints: Stick figures are perfectly fine — the story matters more than the art.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the funniest panel to draw?

quests.title: Family Freeze Dance
quests.summary: Dance together and freeze the instant the music stops.

instructions.text: Clear a small space to move safely.
Play a favorite song and dance together.
Pause the music at random moments — everyone freezes in place until it starts again.

quests.completionPrompt: What was the silliest freeze pose?
quests.safetyNote: Make sure the dance space is clear of furniture and tripping hazards.

quests.title: Animal Movement Challenge
quests.summary: Move around the room like different animals.

instructions.text: Take turns picking an animal — like a bear, crab, frog, or flamingo.
Everyone moves around the room the way that animal would move.
Switch animals every minute or two and see who can guess the next one.

hints: Bear crawls, crab walks, and frog jumps are easy ones to start with.
quests.completionPrompt: Which animal was the hardest to move like?
quests.safetyNote: Clear the space of furniture and other tripping hazards before you start.

quests.title: Notice-Something-New Walk
quests.summary: Take a ten-minute walk together looking for things you've never noticed before.

instructions.text: Head outside together for a short walk around your neighborhood or a nearby park.
As you walk, each person looks for one thing they've never noticed before — a plant, a house detail, a sound.
When you get back, take turns sharing what you each noticed.

quests.completionPrompt: What did your family notice that surprised you?
quests.safetyNote: Stay together as a family and stick to safe, familiar walking areas.

quests.title: Secret Helpful Act
quests.summary: Do one kind, helpful thing for someone in your family without telling them.

instructions.text: Pick one small, helpful task you can do for someone else in your family — like tidying their space or leaving a favorite snack out.
Do it quietly, without saying anything.
See how long it takes them to notice, or wait until they discover it on their own.

hints: Small things count — refilling a water bottle or making a bed both work well.
quests.completionPrompt: How did it feel to help without getting caught?

quests.title: Thank-You Message
quests.summary: Write or draw a thank-you message for someone in your family.

instructions.text: Pick someone in your family to thank for something they did recently.
Write or draw a short thank-you message for them.
Give it to them in person.

hints: If writing is tricky, a drawing works just as well as words.
quests.completionPrompt: What did they say when they read it?

quests.title: Choose Something to Donate
quests.summary: Pick an item together to give away to someone who could use it.

instructions.text: Look through toys, books, or clothes that still work well but aren't used much anymore.
Choose one item together to donate.
Set it aside in a bag ready to give away, and talk about who might enjoy it.

quests.completionPrompt: Who do you imagine will enjoy it next?

quests.title: Sink or Float
quests.summary: Guess and test which household objects sink or float in water.

instructions.text: Fill a bowl or sink with water.
Gather five or six safe household objects, like a spoon, a cork, a coin, or a plastic toy.
Guess whether each one will sink or float, then drop it in and check.
Talk about which guesses were right and which were surprising.

hints: Try comparing objects that look similar in size but are made of different materials.
If something floats but shouldn't, check if it's hollow or sealed with air inside.
quests.completionPrompt: Which result surprised you the most?
quests.safetyNote: Use a bowl or sink, not a bathtub or pool, and stay together during clean-up.

quests.title: Find Something Older Than You
quests.summary: Search your home for an object older than the youngest family member.

instructions.text: Decide whose age you're comparing against — usually the youngest child in the family.
Search around your home for an object that's older than that age.
Bring it back and share what you found and why you think it's that old.

hints: Kitchen drawers, bookshelves, and closets are good places to start looking.
quests.completionPrompt: What's the story behind what you found?

quests.title: Learn Five Words in Another Language
quests.summary: Pick a language and learn five new words together.

instructions.text: Choose a language your family is curious about.
Together, find and learn five simple words or phrases in that language, like hello, thank you, or goodbye.
Practice saying them to each other a few times.
Try using one of the words for the rest of the day.

hints: A phrasebook, dictionary, or a trusted language app all work well for this.
quests.completionPrompt: Which new word was the trickiest to say?

quests.title: Speak Only in Questions
quests.summary: Try to have a whole conversation using only questions.

instructions.text: Pick a simple topic to talk about, like dinner plans or a favorite game.
Everyone can only speak using questions — no statements allowed.
Keep going until someone accidentally makes a statement, then start a new round.

quests.completionPrompt: What was the funniest question anyone asked?

quests.title: Draw Without Looking at the Paper
quests.summary: Draw each other's portraits without ever looking down at the paper.

instructions.text: Sit facing another family member.
Draw their face, but keep your eyes on them the whole time — no looking down at your paper.
Reveal the drawings together when you're both done and compare.

hints: The wobblier the drawing, the funnier the reveal.
quests.completionPrompt: Whose drawing made everyone laugh the most?

quests.title: Invent the Worst Restaurant Menu
quests.summary: Make up the most terrible restaurant menu you can imagine.

instructions.text: Grab a sheet of paper and imagine a restaurant nobody would want to eat at.
Invent silly, terrible-sounding dishes and give the restaurant a name.
Take turns reading the menu out loud in your best waiter voice.

hints: Combining foods that don't belong together is usually the funniest choice.
quests.completionPrompt: Which dish would you never dare order?

quests.title: Recreate an Old Family Photo
quests.summary: Find an old family photo and recreate it together.

instructions.text: Find an old family photo, printed or on a phone or tablet.
Look closely at where everyone is standing, their expressions, and the setting.
Recreate the photo as closely as you can and take a new one.
Place the two photos side by side and compare them.

hints: Don't worry about matching perfectly — close is more fun than exact.
quests.completionPrompt: What's changed the most between the two photos?

quests.title: Tell the Story Behind a Photo
quests.summary: Pick an old photo and tell the story behind it.

instructions.text: Choose an old family photo, printed or on a phone or tablet.
Someone who remembers the moment tells the story behind it — where it was, who's in it, what happened.
Others can ask questions about the details.

quests.completionPrompt: What detail about that day had you forgotten?

quests.title: Map of Important Family Places
quests.summary: Draw a map of the places that matter most to your family.

instructions.text: Get a large sheet of paper and drawing supplies.
Talk together about places that matter to your family — like a favorite park, a grandparent's house, or a special vacation spot.
Draw a simple map marking each place, with a small note about why it matters.

hints: It doesn't need to be geographically accurate — a fun, personal map works best.
quests.completionPrompt: Which place on the map holds the best memory?

quests.title: Draw a Shared Imaginary Creature
quests.summary: Invent a wild, impossible creature together, one feature at a time.

instructions.text: Get one sheet of paper and something to draw with.
Fold the paper into three sections (head, body, legs) — or just draw in turns if you'd rather skip the folding.
Take turns drawing one section without looking at what the others drew.
Unfold or reveal the paper together and give your creature a name and a superpower.

hints: The stranger the creature looks, the better — mismatched parts are half the fun.
quests.completionPrompt: What should your creature's superpower be?

quests.title: Gratitude Paper Chain
quests.summary: Build a paper chain where every link is something your family is thankful for.

instructions.text: Cut several strips of paper, about the width of two fingers.
Each person writes or draws one thing they're grateful for on a strip.
Loop the strips together into a chain, adding new links as you think of more.
Hang the finished chain somewhere everyone will see it.

hints: Keep the chain going over several days — add a new link whenever something good happens.
quests.completionPrompt: Which link on the chain means the most to you?
quests.safetyNote: An adult should handle the scissors for younger children.

quests.title: Design an Indoor Treasure Trail
quests.summary: One family member hides clues around the house for the others to follow.

instructions.text: One person creates a trail of three to five simple written or drawn clues, each leading to the next hiding spot.
Hide a small treasure — like a favorite snack or a handwritten note — at the final spot.
The rest of the family follows the clues together as a team.
Once someone else has had a turn hiding a trail, switch roles.

hints: Clues can be simple, like drawing an arrow or writing a rhyme about the next spot.
quests.completionPrompt: Which clue was the trickiest to figure out?

quests.title: Build a Sculpture from Recyclables
quests.summary: Turn clean recycling into a one-of-a-kind family sculpture.

instructions.text: Gather clean, empty recyclables — cardboard boxes, tubes, bottle caps, egg cartons.
Decide together what to build: an animal, a robot, a building, or something entirely made up.
Tape or glue the pieces together, adding color if you'd like.
Give your finished sculpture a name and a place of honor in your home.

hints: Sturdier materials like cardboard tubes make good arms, legs, or towers.
quests.completionPrompt: What's the best part of your sculpture?
quests.safetyNote: An adult should handle scissors and check that all materials are clean and safe to handle.

quests.title: Invent a Family Handshake
quests.summary: Make up a secret handshake only your family knows.

instructions.text: Stand facing a partner (or take turns if there are more than two of you).
Try out different moves — claps, taps, wiggles, or a fist bump — and pick your favorites.
Put three or four moves together in order and practice until it flows smoothly.
Perform your finished handshake together to celebrate.

hints: Start with just two moves and add more once those feel easy.
quests.completionPrompt: What will you call your handshake?

quests.title: Invent a Mini Board Game
quests.summary: Design your own simple board game from scratch and play it together.

instructions.text: Draw a path of spaces on a sheet of paper, from a start to a finish.
Decide together on simple rules — how to move, and a few fun or silly spaces along the way.
Use coins, buttons, or small toys as game pieces, and a die or number cards to move.
Play your new game as a family, and adjust any rules that aren't working.

hints: Keep the rules short at first — you can always add more once you've played it once.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the funniest space on the board?

quests.title: Ask Each Other Surprising Questions
quests.summary: Take turns asking questions you don't already know the answer to.

instructions.text: Take turns being the asker — everyone else answers.
Ask something you're genuinely curious about, not something you already know the answer to.
Let each person answer fully before moving to the next question.
Keep going as long as the questions keep coming.

hints: Try questions like 'what's something you've never told anyone?' or 'what would your perfect day look like?'
quests.completionPrompt: Which answer surprised you the most?

quests.title: Tell a Story One Sentence at a Time
quests.summary: Build a story together, adding just one sentence each.

instructions.text: One person starts a story with a single sentence.
The next person adds exactly one more sentence, continuing the story.
Keep going around the family, letting the story go wherever it wants.
Decide together when the story has reached a good ending.

hints: It's okay to take the story somewhere silly or unexpected — that's part of the fun.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the most unexpected turn the story took?

quests.title: Recreate a Favorite Family Moment
quests.summary: Act out or retell a favorite memory together, as if it's happening again.

instructions.text: Talk together about a favorite family memory — a trip, a funny mishap, a celebration.
Decide who will play which part, or simply retell it together in as much detail as you can.
Act it out or tell it together, adding in the details you remember.
Talk about what made that moment so memorable.

quests.completionPrompt: What do you remember most vividly about that day?

quests.title: Watch Clouds and Invent Names for Them
quests.summary: Lie back, watch the clouds, and give each shape a name.

instructions.text: Find a comfortable spot outside (or by a window) where you can see the sky.
Take a few quiet minutes just watching the clouds drift by.
Take turns pointing out shapes you see and inventing a name or story for each one.
See if anyone else can spot the same shape before it changes.

hints: No clouds today? Try the same game with the patterns in a ceiling, a rug, or tree branches instead.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the most imaginative cloud shape someone found?
quests.safetyNote: Choose a safe, comfortable spot to sit or lie down, away from traffic.

quests.title: Two Truths and a Wish
quests.summary: Share two true things about yourself and one wish, and see if others can guess which is which.

instructions.text: Each person thinks of two true things about themselves and one wish they have.
Share all three out loud, in any order, without saying which is which.
The rest of the family guesses which one is the wish.
Reveal the answer and talk about why you chose that wish.

quests.completionPrompt: Which wish are you most curious to see come true?

quests.title: Letters to Future Us
quests.summary: Write short letters to your family one year from now.

instructions.text: Give everyone a piece of paper and something to write or draw with.
Write a short letter to your family as it will be one year from today — what you hope for, what you're excited about.
Fold the letters and put them together in an envelope or box.
Write today's date on the outside and store it somewhere safe to open together next year.

hints: Younger family members can draw a picture instead of writing.
quests.completionPrompt: What are you most looking forward to a year from now?

quests.title: Take Turns Leading Family Stretches
quests.summary: Each person leads the family through a few simple stretches.

instructions.text: Stand in a circle with enough space to stretch your arms out.
Take turns being the leader — everyone else copies their stretch.
Hold each stretch for a few slow breaths before switching to the next person.
Finish with everyone's favorite stretch from the round.

hints: Reaching for the sky, touching your toes, and gentle side bends are easy ones to start with.
quests.completionPrompt: Which stretch felt the best?
quests.safetyNote: Stretch gently — no bouncing or forcing a stretch that hurts.

quests.title: Build a Backyard Obstacle Course
quests.summary: Design and build a simple obstacle course together, then try it as a team.

instructions.text: Look around your yard or a nearby safe outdoor space for things to use as obstacles — like stepping around chairs, hopping between spots, or crawling under a table.
Set up three to five stations together, deciding as a family what to do at each one.
Walk through the course together first to make sure it's safe and clear.
Take turns going through the course, cheering each other on.

materials: Household items for obstacles (chairs, cushions, cones)
hints: Keep stations simple and close together so everyone can complete the whole course.
quests.completionPrompt: Which station was the most fun to complete?
quests.safetyNote: Check the space for hazards first and keep obstacles low and stable.

quests.title: Indoor Balloon Volleyball
quests.summary: Keep a balloon off the ground together for as long as you can.

instructions.text: Clear a small space and blow up a balloon.
Decide on a simple boundary, like a couch or a line of tape, to bat the balloon over.
Work together to keep the balloon from touching the ground, counting how many hits you get in a row.
Try to beat your own best count together.

hints: No hands allowed is a fun twist once everyone has the basic game down.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the highest number of hits in a row your family reached?
quests.safetyNote: Keep the play area clear of furniture corners and breakable items. Supervise young children closely around balloons.

quests.title: Sock Skating Challenge
quests.summary: Put on your comfiest socks and invent silly skating moves together.

instructions.text: Find a clear stretch of smooth flooring and put on socks (no shoes).
Take turns gliding across the floor and inventing a silly skating move or pose.
Everyone else copies the move before the next person takes a turn.
Keep going until you've built a whole family skating routine.

hints: Hold onto a wall or counter if you need extra balance.
quests.completionPrompt: Whose skating move was the silliest?
quests.safetyNote: Only play on a clear, non-slippery area away from stairs, and stop if the floor feels too slick.

quests.title: Shadow Puppet Movement Story
quests.summary: Use flashlights and your hands to act out a story in shadows on the wall.

instructions.text: Dim the lights and shine a flashlight or lamp toward a blank wall.
Take turns making shadow shapes with your hands — animals, characters, or made-up creatures.
Use your shadow characters to act out a short story together.
Take a bow together when the story ends.

hints: A rabbit is one of the easiest shadow shapes to start with — two fingers up for ears.
quests.completionPrompt: What was your shadow story about?

quests.title: Backyard Relay Challenge
quests.summary: Work together as a team to complete a simple relay course.

instructions.text: Set up a short course in your yard or a nearby open space, like running to a tree and back.
Decide on one fun movement for the relay, like hopping, crab-walking, or skipping.
Take turns completing the course, passing an object like a scarf or ball to the next person.
Cheer each other on and celebrate finishing together as a team.

hints: Focus on completing the relay together rather than timing it — teamwork is the point.
quests.completionPrompt: What was the funniest way someone moved through the course?
quests.safetyNote: Choose a flat, open space away from roads and check for tripping hazards first.

quests.title: Blanket Fort Campout Night
quests.summary: Build a blanket fort and spend an evening camping out inside it together.

instructions.text: Gather blankets, pillows, and chairs, and build a fort in your living room or bedroom.
Bring in flashlights, cozy blankets, and a few favorite books or games.
Spend the evening together inside the fort — tell stories, read, or just talk.
If you'd like, let everyone stay the night inside the fort.

materials: Chairs or furniture to build the frame
hints: Chairs pushed together with blankets draped over the top make a sturdy, roomy fort.
quests.completionPrompt: What was your favorite part of your night in the fort?
quests.safetyNote: Keep the fort away from candles or any open flame, and make sure furniture used is stable.

quests.title: Neighborhood Photo Scavenger Hunt
quests.summary: Walk your neighborhood together, photographing everything on a shared list.

instructions.text: Make a list together of five to eight things to look for on a walk, like a red door, a friendly dog, or an interesting tree.
Head out together and take a photo of each item as a family when you spot it.
Check items off the list together as you find them.
Look back through your photos together when you get home.

hints: Let the youngest family member help decide what goes on the list.
quests.completionPrompt: Which item was the hardest to find?
quests.safetyNote: Stay together as a family, stick to familiar sidewalks and crossings, and be mindful of traffic.

quests.title: Plan a Small Act of Kindness
quests.summary: Choose someone to surprise with a small act of kindness and plan it together.

instructions.text: Talk together about someone you could surprise with kindness — a neighbor, a relative, or a friend.
Decide together what you'll do, like making a card, baking something, or helping with a task.
Prepare it together as a family.
Deliver or share it, either in person or by leaving it somewhere they'll find it.

materials: Depends on what you plan (paper and art supplies help)
hints: Keep it simple — a handwritten card or a small favor means just as much as something elaborate.
quests.completionPrompt: How do you think it made them feel?

quests.title: Backyard Picnic Adventure
quests.summary: Pack a simple picnic and turn your own yard into an adventure spot.

instructions.text: Pack a simple picnic together — snacks, drinks, and a blanket to sit on.
Choose a spot in your yard, a balcony, or a nearby park to set up.
Enjoy your picnic together, and invent a game or story to go with your 'adventure' location.
Pack everything back up together when you're done.

hints: Give your picnic spot an adventurous name, like 'Base Camp' or 'The Secret Grove.'
quests.completionPrompt: What would you name your picnic adventure?

quests.title: Make a Weekend Mini-Adventure Map
quests.summary: Plan and draw a map of a small adventure to go on together this weekend.

instructions.text: Talk together about a few nearby places you could visit in an afternoon — a park, a trail, a new street to explore.
Draw a simple map together showing the route and stops along the way.
Head out and follow your map together.
Mark your map with notes about what you found at each stop.

hints: Keep the adventure small and close to home — the map is what makes it feel like an expedition.
quests.completionPrompt: What would you add to the map next time?

quests.title: Make a Family Time Capsule
quests.summary: Fill a box with small items and notes to open together in the future.

instructions.text: Find a small box or container to use as your time capsule.
Each person adds one or two small items or notes — a drawing, a favorite small object, or a written memory from this year.
Write the date on the outside and agree together on when to open it, like in one or five years.
Store it somewhere safe until that day comes.

hints: Photos, ticket stubs, or a handwritten note about this year all make great additions.
quests.completionPrompt: What are you most excited to rediscover when you open it?
